newsitem.title: LEBANON: Israelis shell south Lebanon town, cause damage.
newsitem.headline: Israelis shell south Lebanon town, cause damage.

text.p: Israeli forces fired at a group of guerrillas in south Lebanon on Thursday night and some of the shells slammed into the market town of Nabatiyeh, causing damage but no casualties, security sources said.

They said a number of shells hit the Maslakh area in the town which is just north of Israel's south Lebanon occupation zone. The shells caused some damage to houses and a woman fainted as a result of the bombardment, they added.

Launching attacks at or from civilian areas is barred under a U.S.-brokered ceasefire understanding that ended a 17-day Israeli blitz on Lebanon last April in which some 200 people, mostly civilians, were killed.
The sources said guerrillas in the Nabatiyeh area also fired mortar bombs at Israeli posts overlooking the town.
Sources with the Israeli-backed South Lebanon Army (SLA) militia said Israeli helicopters fired rockets and heavy machineguns at a group of guerrillas in Kfar Roumane near Nabatiyeh.
Israeli gunners also fired artrillery shells at the guerrillas. It was not immediately known if there were any casualites on either side.
The ceasefire understanding allows attacks by pro-Iranian Hizbollah and other guerrillas against Israeli forces in south Lebanon and gives both sides the right to self defence.
Hizbollah (Party of God) is fighting to oust some 1,000 Israeli troops and 3,000 SLA militiamen from the south Lebanon zone set up to prevent cross-frontier raids on northern Israel.
